Speaking as someone who had to emigrate, many years ago now, and was fortunate enough to be able to come back -   You certainly don't speak for me. I don't feel any 'slap in the face' at the hearing of the phrase. I 100% concur with the idea that 'Ireland is Full'.  Because it certainly is from the point of view of the strain on our essential services. And that is what we mean by saying so. At least you didn't trot out the old 'we had 9 million before the famine' BS.  We are not, in 2025 Ireland, bound by our history of emigration. Absolutely not, that would be an absurd impediment to our right to choose our own destiny. And all that is before you even dissect the shallowness of the comparison.   It is irrelevant whether or not immigrants are to blame for 'wanting a better life for themselves'. Of course they do. But we are not obliged to dis-improve our standard of living for that reason.  We have increased our population in thirty very short years by about 50%. Too much, arguably. And yet without hardly an ounce of bother, Brits, Poles, Brazilians all came here in huge numbers, and we all got along.  Different game now. Not all immigration is equal, nor equally beneficial to US. And that is the ultimate measure.  The idea that there is no link between immigration and accommodation is Leftwaffe nonsense. What you might call rhetoric. David McWilliams has dealt with this very connection in his podcast, last July. Listen and learn.  And Ireland Is Full.

However what we don’t have is housing and infrastructure and that can make it *feel* like it’s at breaking point.   But you only need to look around the countryside out west to see the traces of a much bigger rural population. You only need to walk around *any* town or village away from a big city to find empty/unoccupied buildings. There is plenty of space, we are an under-occupied country in need of a larger tax base, a more diverse economy and a more ambitious spatial strategy.  If we had the confidence to actually aim for a population size by 2050 and say “we *want* to be a country of 10 million by then, we now need to remove the obstacles towards reaching that. We have plenty of immigration but we also need to make having kids easier. We could be a very happy country with twice the population. I think you’re confusing immigration with asylum, to come to Ireland as an immigrant and get a job you need a visa, and the visa process includes vetting.  Also, only immigrants with a residency status (meaning they’ve already been vetted and work for years) can claim social benefits such as housing. What you see in hotels, etc are asylum seekers coming from Ukraine and other countries in crisis, and Ireland as part of the EU and other international treaties has to receive them. These people are not allowed to work because they’re here temporarily. Only some are granted permission to remain and to obtain that, there is also a vetting process. So, before you start saying that nothing is controlled and borders are open to everyone to come in a take free accommodation and other benefits from Irish people, you should be better informed.  Signed, an immigrant living legally in Ireland for 12 years, who went through all the vetting and is now a citizen and has never obtained one cent from social welfare.
